chapter: Dew Drop and the name Red
title: Pay and atmosphere at the Dew Drop
summary: The Dew Drop paid about eight dollars, was a sit-down club, and drinks were cheap; the room later moved to the back.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And, uh, uh, uh, so, yes, uh, did, uh, were you ever, did, did, did, did the Dew Drop, shows like the Dew Drop pay very well?

Uh, they played, paid, uh, I imagine what was the going rate, about eight bucks. Mm-hmm. Which is about what the union called for, back during that, that time. You have to take into consideration that, as I can recall, uh, guys would come in with their dates, and it was a sit-down club, uh, tables and waitresses. Right. And a guy who could drink, or was a drinker, he could get a half a pint of whiskey, uh, a Coke and a seven-up set-up with a bowl of ice and lemon and cherries for $1.75. That, that was common at the Dew Drop?
I mean, that was generally the set-up? Yeah. Did, did, did, did, did, did, did people at the Dew Drop dance? Was it a dance play?
Oh, there was some, there was some, uh, um, people that would dance, but it was more of a sit-down. Yeah.
Yeah. Even though, yeah, that's, I've always thought that, the Drop, it was more of a sit-down play. Yeah.
Yeah. You sat, you drank, and you watched.
You held hands, or you did whatever you did.

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. And that's the way it was, uh, and, uh, from time to time, it would shift from the front, where we played mostly. Mm-hmm. And then at a time when I played with Dave Bartholomew, they had moved it in the back where they had a, uh, a bigger seating space and a bigger bandstand. And I played that with Dave later.
